title: keyDown / keyUp
description: One physical key going down or up, on the `keys` channel -- NOT the `input` channel. Keys ride an ordered, reliable channel of their own because typing needs every keystroke exactly once and in order, which is the opposite of what pointer samples want; see catalog.json `channels`. Unlike pointer messages these are events, not state: there is no seq and no held-key mask, because the channel already guarantees order and delivery. The key is identified by its POSITION (DOM KeyboardEvent.code), never by the character it produces -- the host maps the position to its own native key and lets its own keyboard layout decide the character, exactly like a plugged-in keyboard. That is what keeps two machines with different layouts, dead keys and AltGr correct without either side knowing the other's layout.

code.description: DOM KeyboardEvent.code, e.g. KeyA, Digit1, ShiftLeft, MetaLeft, NumpadEnter. Positions, so MetaLeft is the Windows key on a PC keyboard and Command on a Mac one -- the host maps by position (Win <-> Command, Alt <-> Option). A code the host has no key for (F24 on a Mac) is counted and dropped, never guessed at.

repeat.description: keyDown only: an autorepeat generated by the SENDER's OS while the key is held. Neither host autorepeats a synthesised key, so these are forwarded rather than regenerated -- which keeps the repeat rate the user configured on the machine in front of them. Absent means false.
